concerns.text: Task T018a implements a '5-Fold Greedy Maximal Dissimilarity Split' loop. This contradicts FR-004 in spec.md which mandates a single 'maximal dissimilarity split' to create a held-out test set. The task silently relaxes the spec's structural constraint by replacing a single split with K-fold CV, altering the fundamental experimental design defined in the spec.

Task T025c3 requires calculating and reporting 'Mean Gini Importance' (normalized by bit count) while claiming the 'Absolute Sum' is the validation metric. SC-003 in spec.md explicitly defines the metric as 'The sum of Gini importance... must exceed... by ≥ 15%'. Introducing a normalized 'Mean' metric as a primary output creates a semantic drift where the reported value does not match the spec's defined success criterion, risking incorrect validation.

Tasks T025a, T025b, and T029a2 mandate performing statistical tests (t-test, bootstrap CI) and generating tables for 'Precision-Recall AUC' (PR-AUC). While Constitution Principle VII mentions reporting PR-AUC, FR-005 and SC-001 in spec.md strictly define the statistical validation (Corrected Resampled t-test) and success criteria solely around 'ROC-AUC'. The tasks silently expand the statistical scope to PR-AUC without explicit spec authorization, violating the constraint that the t-test applies to the specific metric defined in FR-005.
